summary: Turn 13. Map v4 was accepted and the previous candidates are explained; this turn resolves the active A7 client-correlation Candidate 3de2a473694c4613ab082d19bdde9d54 as explained by the server's reply ordering. Sourced reasoning: runSingleClient sets Leaderless=true and Fast=false for epaxos, so every proposal from one client goes to ClosestId (client/client.go:175-196) and lands in that one replica's own row with consecutive instances (epaxos/epaxos.go:724-749). Dreply is true (replica/replica.go:94), so the coordinator's commit-time replies are skipped (the !Dreply branches at epaxos/epaxos.go:931 and 1044) and the only reply path is execution, where shouldRespond replies per command in w.Cmds order (epaxos/exec.go:119-140). Within the proposing replica's row execution is head-driven — executeCommands walks each row from ExecedUpTo+1 and stops at the first non-executable instance (epaxos/epaxos.go:385-435) — and a same-row instance cannot be a dependency of an earlier one, so same-row instances are never mutual SCC members and are executed and answered in increasing instance order, with batched proposals replying in cmds order. Arrival order therefore equals request order for one client, so B-CLIENT-OBSERVE's missing identity check has no observable consequence in the modelled leaderless client, and no defect is claimed. Submitted action=explained with the question (disposition explained_by_existing_mechanism, audit_spec_version 4, activity_classes A7 with supported A1, principal fact F-CLIENT-REPLY-LINK, direct behavior B-CLIENT-OBSERVE, supporting B-CLIENT-REPLY / B-CLIENT-ISSUE / B-EXEC / B-PROPOSE, obligation_relation_kind consumption). Counterevidence keeps the latent gap visible (the CommandId is preserved and could be matched but is not, and the source's own TODO records the unchecked comparison) and remaining records the residual questions: whether any supported configuration (multi-replica client, Dreply=false, per-RPC replies) can reorder replies, the still-unchecked A1 fast path and A2 authority transitions, unread A4 membership and A6 durability, and the earlier Accept-reply latency/ballot-range residual. Preflight validation returns valid=true; formal acceptance and any execution remain the controller's.
